links.comparator_used: Manual search of the Chinese Human Phenotype Ontology website by junior physicians, with no MLLM prompts
links.outcome: Accuracy of HPO term identification from patient images, compared with an expert panel standard set
links.effect: MLLM-assisted 67.4% (182/270) vs manual 20.4% (55/270); relative risk 3.31, 95% CI 2.58-4.25; P<.001
links.tradeoff: The MLLMs hallucinated often. ChatGPT-4o gave incorrect HPO IDs in 57.3% (67/117) of cases and fabricated terms in 34.2% (40/117). The open-source Llama models had incorrect IDs in 82-98% of cases.
links.quote: The MLLM-assisted group achieved a significantly higher accuracy rate of 67.4% (182/270) compared to 20.4% (55/270) in the manual group (relative risk 3.31, 95% CI 2.58-4.25; P<.001).

design_hint: clinician verification of MLLM-suggested HPO terms via database search
